# Synthetic adoption predecessor

These gzip-compressed PostgreSQL custom archives are test data for the one supported v113-to-baseline adoption. They were built in independent disposable PostgreSQL 16 clusters from revision `d34acea2ac0938b005cae962a62591c20b69084d`, with the source-defined empty, ordinary-synthetic and prepared-runner setup paths. They contain schema/installation metadata and either no fixture rows or the original 277 explicitly synthetic fixture records plus the synthetic EPSS connection. No development database, tenant, runner or live lab supplied these archives. Global roles and passwords are not included by `pg_dump`; test provisioning supplies isolated role credentials.

`manifest.json` records compressed/uncompressed SHA-256, the original database annotation and source provenance. Restoring PostgreSQL definitions reparses the four documented equivalent definitions into the trusted current layout; the original predecessor installation record is retained for adoption tests. Tests must verify archive hashes and restore only into their disposable isolated clusters. These fixtures replace executing the historical migration chain in adoption tests; they do not reintroduce older deployed-version support. Recorded source revisions remain provenance identifiers; the approved history cleanup removes those old Git objects from named repository refs. Tests use these bundled, hash-verified fixtures rather than retrieving historical migration source.

The ordinary synthetic predecessor also has one independently reproduced installation-signature variant: reader ACL entries precede fixture-role entries in five `tables` rows and 55 `relation_authority` rows. Swapping only those two entries in those arrays from this frozen synthetic archive reproduces the additional complete signature hash in `predecessor-metadata.json`. The archives themselves remain unchanged. `test_predecessor_signature.py` reconstructs the variant from the archive, checks the exact hash and rejects additional ordering, permission, ownership or definition changes. Live catalogue/authority, source artifacts and annotation checks remain mandatory; no arbitrary signature normalization is accepted.
